clue.text: Cry from the 8, perhaps: "Bosom OK! Is m' behind guilty?"

annotation.answer: DOES MY BUM LOOK BIG IN THIS

blocks.clueFragment: Bosom OK! Is m' behind guilty
blocks.note: every letter of the quoted words is used once

explanation.surface: Someone in a changing room asks, cheekily, whether their bottom is up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram signal: the quotation itself is the jumbled form of the cry. The 8 is 8 Down, CHANGING ROOMS, where clothes are tried on.
explanation.definitionFit: This anxious question is the classic thing shoppers ask companions while trying on clothes in a fitting cubicle.

clue.text: All eyes, all eyes are here at Lord's

definitions.text: all eyes are here at Lord's

blocks.note: first meaning: fully alert and attentive

blocks.clueFragment: all eyes are here at Lord's
blocks.note: second meaning: where spectators look during a cricket match

explanation.surface: Spectators at a cricket match are all watching intently.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground; during play everyone watches the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and quick to react is an idiom; literally, spectators' gaze rests on the cricket ball.

clue.text: The setter's cunning without being ingratiating

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece sits around the other

blocks.note: sly means crafty
the setter is I, so the setter's is I'm

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being clever without stooping to flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here has its old sense of outside, as in the hymn's 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unpleasantly fawning and oily in manner is described informally with this word.

clue.text: Defer one's return

blocks.note: first meaning: give way to another
second meaning: the profit an investment produces

explanation.surface: Someone postpones coming back home.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way is to submit to another; the income produced by an investment is also called by this word.

clue.text: Illiterate members of NUT routed

indicators.note: an army that is routed is scattered in disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the indicator word also supplies letters

explanation.surface: Teachers' union members are mocked as unable to read after a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT is Britain's National Union of Teachers, which makes 'illiterate' a joke. 'Routed' works both as fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without schooling or formal instruction has not been taught, hence lacking education and reading skill.

clue.text: Speaking of loo brush head, right? I can't find a smoother!

indicators.note: speaking points to how the following words sound when said rather than how they are written
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: loo is British slang for a lavatory; the sound is spelt differently
first letter of brush
R is the usual abbreviation for right
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone with a toilet brush complains they cannot find anything to smooth things.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, LOO-B-R-I-CAN'T is the answer: LUBRICANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil or grease reduces friction, making surfaces slide more easily, so it acts as something that smooths.

clue.text: One arresting copper at the right time

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold or seize, so the first word holds the next inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A person detaining a police officer just when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor entering exactly when prompted arrives punctually; the phrase means at precisely the appropriate moment.

clue.text: One of the BBC's trying habits here

blocks.note: first meaning: a home-makeover television programme
second meaning: cubicles where garments are tried on

explanation.surface: A BBC series full of annoying habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The title was a popular BBC show in which neighbours redecorated each other's rooms. 'Trying habits' means trying on clothes, not irritating behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A television programme of that title, and the shop or sports-club cubicles where people try on outfits.

clue.text: Pi? Look at it this way; its Hell!

blocks.clueFragment: Pi? Look at it this way
blocks.note: surface reading: an odd remark about the mathematical constant

blocks.clueFragment: Pi? Look at it this way
blocks.note: setter's reading: a three-letter hole with its lowest letter cut off leaves PI

explanation.surface: Someone explains pi with a different perspective, then shrugs that it is hell.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the bottom of PIT is its T; remove it and PI is left, so PI is a pit without a bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The abyss of the damned in the Bible's Book of Revelation is described as an endless chasm.

clue.text: Head-to-head link for burning issues

blocks.note: first meaning: a direct line between heads of state
second meaning: a phone service for urgent matters, with hot read as burning

explanation.surface: A direct channel between leaders for dealing with urgent questions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Washington–Moscow direct telephone link was so named, and helplines for urgent public concerns share the term.

clue.text: Old, cold Bostonian, who speaks only to God, returning to Virginia

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the string is read right to left

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
C for cold, as on a tap

blocks.clueFragment: Bostonian, who speaks only to God
blocks.note: from the rhyme: the Lowells talk only to Cabots, and the Cabots talk only to God

explanation.surface: An elderly, aloof Boston grandee travels back south to Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cabots are a Boston Brahmin family, famously snobbish in the old toast about Boston. 'Virginia' looks like the destination but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a well-known variety of leaf for smoking, grown originally in that American state.

clue.text: Born, die, unknown, bereft

blocks.note: née, used before a woman's maiden name, means born
d. is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
y is one of the unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A bleak obituary: born, died, nobody knew them, and left with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deprived and lacking the necessities of life is poor and in want, in a state of hardship.

clue.text: Tired out, chaps? Take time handicap!

indicators.note: out as in worn out or out of shape, so the letters are put in disarray

blocks.note: taken as written
chaps are men
T for time

explanation.surface: Exhausted men are told to accept a time penalty in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or damage that holds someone back acts as a disadvantage, the sense the noun shares with the clue word.

clue.text: Issue from Abraham's tax-free investment account

blocks.note: an ISA is a British tax-free Individual Savings Account
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A payout from a man's tax-free savings plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks financial, but means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the son born to Abraham and Sarah in old age bore this name; issue means children.

clue.text: Madly macerates sustenance from Devon?

indicators.note: doing something madly means doing it wildly and without order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frantically soaks food to make a West Country snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is an English county famous for scones with clotted cream and jam served with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones, clotted cream, jam and a pot of tea are the classic refreshment associated with that south-western county.

clue.text: De Brunhoff's elephantine ignorance?

blocks.note: Jean de Brunhoff created Babar the elephant, so his elephant's way of being is a Babar-ism

explanation.surface: A children's author's elephant hero is accused of being ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no 'say' signal; the question mark flags the pun. In a non-rhotic British accent, with the r's silent, the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of culture or civilised learning is crude uncultivated behaviour, a sense of ignorance in the old usage.

clue.text: See 1
Pussy's place with Ellen Marshal?

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order, so the letters are lined up afresh

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Where a cat might be found, together with a woman called Ellen Marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: From the nursery rhyme 'Ding dong bell, pussy's in the well'. Marshal looks like Ellen's surname but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the cat has fallen down a water shaft, so that is where the pussy is.

clue.text: If good for hard investment, could be delighted with money-back guarantee

indicators.note: one thing for another means it stands in place of it
could be suggests another possible form, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
G for good
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A safe investment would make anyone pleased, especially with a refund promise.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the H in delighted for a G, then rearrange. Gilt-edged stocks are British government bonds, the 'investment' of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Government securities are considered utterly safe, so the term describes anything carrying a very reliable assurance of repayment.

clue.text: Decimation of congregation's the duty of the church

blocks.note: first meaning: a tenth taken from worshippers
second meaning: the levy owed to the church

explanation.surface: Thinning a church's flock sounds like the clergy's grim obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: Decimation literally means taking one in ten; here it is a tenth of the congregation's income, not a massacre.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce or earnings, paid as a levy to support clergy, was a traditional obligation of parishioners.

clue.text: Graces Roman sent packing

indicators.note: sent packing suggests scattered and dismissed, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Graces were sent away by a Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graces' looks like the mythological sisters, but it is a verb meaning adorns.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean decorates or adorns something, adding beauty and embellishment to it.

clue.text: Anacreon's interior decoration material

indicators.note: interior means the inside part, so the letters sit inside the name

blocks.note: the inner letters of the Greek poet's name

explanation.surface: The interior décor in a Greek poet's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Anacreon was an ancient Greek lyric poet; 'interior decoration' reads as one phrase but is split.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is the iridescent lining of shells, used for inlays and ornamental work.

clue.text: Namely, a poem: one from Wells's pen?

blocks.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means namely
If is Kipling's famous poem
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A poem, perhaps written by H. G. Wells.
explanation.walkthrough: H. G. Wells wrote The Time Machine and The War of the Worlds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells was a pioneer of speculative fiction about time travel and alien invasion, so his writing belongs to that genre.

clue.text: Born under cross

blocks.note: b. is the abbreviation for born
less than, below in amount

explanation.surface: Someone born under the sign of the cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a noun or 'angry', but is the verb: to make the sign of the cross over.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest gives a blessing by making the sign of the cross, so to cross someone is to sanctify them.

clue.text: Here Hebrideans run in to back a horse

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the word is read from the end
put in means placed inside something else

blocks.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
R for run, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Islanders dash in to place a bet on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides off the west of Scotland. 'Back a horse' sounds like betting.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an island in the Outer Hebrides, so it is a place where some Hebrideans live.

clue.text: Morpheus's murderer?

blocks.note: surface reading: whoever killed the god of dreams
setter's reading: Morpheus stands for sleep, and Shakespeare's Scottish king is told he does murder sleep

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play a voice cries that the title character 'does murder sleep'; Morpheus is the Greek god of sleep and dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's usurping king, after killing Duncan, is said to have slain sleep itself, the realm Morpheus rules.

clue.text: Citizen demanding one's right to a priest

blocks.note: one is I, so one's is I's
R for right
taken as written
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A citizen insists on their right to see a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of the Jewish state founded in 1948 is a citizen of that Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Not the most fitting abuse, as little changes

indicators.note: whatever changes takes a different form, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Insults are hardly appropriate, since they change little.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of unfitness is the opposite of most appropriate; both describe the worst match for a purpose.
